reviews.comment: Sweet but a difficult accent. Lectures r her reading off slides. Has trouble understanding qs smtimes. Attendance for grade w/ 25% grace(almost never went after a month). zybooks & HW (almost all free 100(manage time!)). Exams not too challenging & final can replace exam grade. First half is basics but second is harder. No extra credit or curves.

Lectures are horrible, she just reads off the slides. The slides themselves are ok, but you pretty much have to learn everything yourself unless you go to office hours. She is so nice in office hours and will give good feedback and advice. Exams are hard, but she curves. You get extra points on your final grade for perfect attendance.

She's a good professor. The lectures aren't very engaging, but at least she doesn't make you use LaTeX, which gives her a big bonus. Class is difficult, and the content isn't very easy to understand since a lot of it is theoretical, but if you're really good at math logic, it shouldn't be too bad. Do not underestimate the course.

120/121 is a difficult class. Lectures were alright, but having other profs lectures help a lot. Seemed to freeze up whenever she was asked a question and didn't quite answer it. She does know a lot about coding. Office hours include all profs and TAs from all sections. First half of the course is easy. Second half everything spikes in difficulty.
Okay prof, shes nice but confusing lectures
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures, personally, were not helpful. The examples on her slides were so hard with barely any explanation and her explaining during lectures can be confusing. If you struggle to understand lectures with a foreign professor, don't take her. But she is super nice and the tests aren't graded too harshly.

This was a hard class and it was just made harder by the professor. She has a heavy accent and a lot of the time can't understand the students. The lectures were so confusing I had to learn it outside of class even though I went to every lecture. She has a high grade distribution, but you are going to be confused and lost most of the time.

Huang's class is very lecture-heavy, and sometimes it can be a little difficult to follow along. Homework is given weekly and expands upon the concepts learned in the lectures. However, she was extremely accessible and was always willing to help out after class. Exams were extremely difficult, but she is generous with partial credit.

Huang was OK for 222, The hardest part about this class was just generally knowing what was going to be on the exams as she would only state the topics, not specific questions. Gives 2 bonus pts at the end of sem if you attend all classes. Exam 1 ez, Exam 2 curved don't slack off, Final OK. DO NOT STOP PAYING ATTENTION, YOU"LL PLAY CATCHUP FOR LONG

Huang was OK for 222, The hardest part about this class was just generally knowing what was going to be on the exams as she would only state the topics, not specific questions. Gives 2 bonus points at the end of the semester if you attend all classes so make sure to do that. Exam 1 ez, Exam 2 curved don't slack off, Final OK.

This prof is incredibly hard to understand. Because of this she also has a hard time understanding her students. She doesn't give clear examples and is not able to explain how she is solving her problems. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROF FOR 222

huang has a rlly strong accent thats hard to understand and isn't engaging. lecture slides r good. sometimes she takes attendance with a google form (id say roughly once every 1-2 weeks). full attendance equals +2 pts on final average which is nice. hw is an enjoyable amount (5 q/week). hw is harder than exams. exams r graded super leniently.

Would not recommend her as a professor...I've always had some trouble understanding discrete math, but I'm taking her class right now and it is difficult. She's great at explaining the basics (propositional logic, sets, etc.) but when we got into the more complex topics it is impossible. Having to completely rely on YouTube videos.
Not a good lecturer. Nobody in the class was engaged.
If you take her be ready to study a lot on your own because the lectures can be confusing and the tests are very difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Terrible lecturer. Hard to understand, moves way to fast, gives no context or application of material. The class is fairly easy due to the material, but she is awful at teaching. People only come to class for attendance and no one pays any attention to her because you are better off watching a youtube video on the material.

Dr. Huang is very sweet, and for her first time teaching 221, she didnt do too bad. Her accent is sometimes unclear, and she is a bit disorganized with her lectures. Homeworks and labs were reasonable and the TA's were godsent when it came to the programming assignments. She is super approachable and its not too hard to teach yourself the concepts/
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: She is very kind and clearly cares about her students, but is not terribly clear about what she expects from students on assignments. Last two exams were on paper (handwritten coding questions - yuck) and entirely free response, but there was very minimal partial credit given, which blows. Most grading done at last minute, long after due dates.

Professor Huang is great as a person, but not so much as a teacher. She really tries to help the students out in terms of grade (like she will curve bad testes). I stopped attending her lectures the last 3 weeks of the semester, since she does post the slides. Pop quizzes were the most surprising, but just make sure you have some good classmates.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Huang is an excellent professor for DSA. She explains thoroughly each process of an algorithm in her lectures. She, although, talks quietly and has a slight accent; which sometimes made it hard to understand Dr. Huang. Her homework and programming assignments were quite doable and she gives a lot of time . Only complain are her pop quizzes.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Huang is an exemplary pedagogue whose adroitness in imparting the nuances of discrete mathematics leaves an indelible impression. Her lucidly orchestrated lectures, replete with cogent explications is laudable. Her contagious zeal for the subject engenders a positive and nurturing ambiance, fostering a love for learning! Bravo.
Dr. Huang was the best professor that I had this year. I had her for 121 and 222. She is really good and nice.
Dr. Huang is one of the best professors at Texas A&M. Take her if you get the chance.

Dr. Huang is a wonderful professor for 221. She makes DSA easy and fun and has a very manageable workload. Other 221 profs have you doing hours of programming assignments, but Dr. Huang offers a much more manageable homework load paired with excellent instruction. She is the best 221 prof if you want to learn and get an A! Kindest CSCE Prof too.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Dr. Huang made 222 easy. She is a theoretical computer scientist so her understanding of Discrete Mathematics is very strong and that translates directly to her lecture. She is kind + always available even outside of her office hours. She was very accommodating throughout the semester. 

TL:DR; Take Dr. Huang!! She's the best prof for 222
Dr. Huang is a gem for CSCE 120/121 if you can take her, take her. Your grade and learning will thank you for years to come. Hope Dr. Huang stays with A&M for years to come

She has a slight accent, but I had no trouble understanding her. She is one of the nicest professors I have had and is always trying to help students understand what is going on in her class. She is a new professor which can show in her lectures, but she is clearly trying and always stops to take questions. She is also a very light grader!

This was her first semester teaching and you could tell. However, her teaching greatly improved at the end of the year once she figured out what she needed to do. She has an accent but I didn't really have any trouble understanding her. Super nice and very easy to reach out to. This class is standardized so her class is just as hard as the others.

Prof. Huang's communication (both of class content and class logistics) isn't always clear. However, she is very committed to helping those who want to learn. She has lots of office hours and posts resources in canvas that are helpful when working on labs/hw/exam prep.

Professor Huang's lectures honestly weren't that helpful for me, so I frequently skipped. The complication to this is that the participation grade for her sections is based off of a few pop quizzes. She did seem to genuinely care about her students and made herself available outside of classes, especially before the final, to help out.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Huang is a very kind person who genuinely cares about her students. However her lectures tend to be boring and confusing. The homework is quite difficult. The tests are only 15 points. To her credit she holds several office hours and posts answers to the hw to help students. If you are ok learning on your own take her but I wouldn't recommend.

Dr.Huang is an incredibly kind and caring professor and it is clear from spending time in class with her that she is passionate about what she does. I. One criticism I have is that she moves equally fast through all of the course material regardless of difficulty, but outside of that had a great experience.

I had Dr Huang for CSCE 121 and 222 concurrently. She is bad at communicating effectively and could be much more organized. Canvas messages to the class are often unclear and/or unnecessary and lectures are very rarely helpful but she throws in quizzes to make you attend. Avoid this prof especially in 222 as most policies are up to each professor.
Best option for this class!

I started learning how to code this semester and Dr. Huang made this course much easier. Even on the weekends/at midnight, she would respond to my emails very fast. Although she is hard to understand in class, she is incredibly helpful 1-on-1. CSCE 120/121 has a very heavy course load, be prepared to invest a lot of time and attend office hours!

Huang is the kindest, most lenient professor I have ever had. She is incredibly helpful in office hours and through email (where she would respond incredibly fast, even on weekends). Her in class quizzes are random, so attending class is important. The only reason I gave her a 4/5 is because of the language barrier; however, it isn't that bad.

Great class! And she is so caring and friendly! She wants you to succeed and is helpful during office hours!
This class is difficult and the homeworks are very long, but that is just because the class is taught by lots of professors. She is definitely the best option out of the professors available for a tough class.

It was her first-semester teaching as a professor but I did not learn a single thing. The lecture was impossible to pay attention too because she does not speak English well at all and she talked too softly. I lived in the Peterson peer teacher help desk during the semester because I was underprepared for the labs

You will have to teach yourself ALL material covered in this class. She speaks (at best) broken English and can't/won't answer questions in lectures. The ONLY way to be successful in her class is by combining the Zybooks info, knowledge from other Professors/TAs/PTs (if you're lucky), and lots of hard work. Good luck, you will need it.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader
